item.title: North Sea Offshore Wind Hubs Draw $14 Billion in Private HVDC Transmission Capital
item.description:
ROTTERDAM — A consortium of Nordic pension funds and infrastructure lenders committed $14.2 billion this week to finance high-voltage direct current (HVDC) converter stations linking offshore wind arrays directly to coastal chemical and steel complexes.

For more than a decade, subsea grid links lagged behind turbine construction because regulated utilities lacked balance-sheet headroom to absorb multi-year permitting delays. The new merchant-regulated hybrid concessions guarantee minimum availability payments while splitting congestion rents between port authorities and institutional bondholders.
